english.title: Supply a psychoactive substance
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally supplied a psychoactive substance, namely **(..IDENTIFY SUBSTANCE..), to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) when you knew or suspected, or ought to have known or suspected, that it was a psychoactive substance, knowing or being reckless as to whether it was likely to be consumed by the person to whom it was supplied, or by some other person, for its psychoactive effects
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 5(1) and 10(1) of the Psychoactive Substances Act 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally supply a substance to another
the substance was psychoactive substance
knows / suspects / ought to know / suspect the substance was psychoactive substance
knows / was reckless as to whether substance likely to be consumed for psychoactive effects

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Where this offence was committed near school premises, by using a courier under the age of 18 or within a custodial institution, section 72 of the Sentencing Act 2020 provides that this has to be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine

Note: If the offence was committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 'Twelve months' to be read as 'Six months'.

Time Limit for Prosecution:
None
